instruction: Export the open blog articles as PDF files named after their titles, and save them in /home/user/Documents/Blog.

metadata.explanation: Task requires saving two blog pages as PDFs with filenames matching titles. The evaluator checks if PDFs contain specific distinguishing keywords from each blog post to ensure correct content mapping. Score is proportional to percentage of keywords found per file. Each file has 5 unique keywords that verify the correct blog content was saved to the correct file.

scoring_breakdown.0.0: No PDF files or no keywords found
scoring_breakdown.0.2: 2 out of 10 keywords found in their correct files
scoring_breakdown.0.5: 5 out of 10 keywords found in their correct files
scoring_breakdown.0.8: 8 out of 10 keywords found in their correct files
scoring_breakdown.1.0: All 10 keywords found in their correct files (5 per PDF)

llm_judge_reasons: Per-file keyword verification correctly implemented (metrics/pdf.py:26-32): Each keyword is verified to be in its corresponding file, ensuring correct file-to-content mapping.
Distinctive keywords chosen: Each blog has 5 unique keywords (titles, technical terms) that are unlikely to appear in the wrong blog, providing good content verification.
Proportional scoring logic is semantically correct: Score = found_keywords / total_keywords, appropriate for multi-file task with partial credit.
Getter implementation is robust: Handles file existence checks, uses PyMuPDF for text extraction, handles errors gracefully with empty list returns.
Minor limitation: Requires exact filename match rather than fuzzy title matching, but this is acceptable given the instruction specifies exact titles.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding fuzzy filename matching to handle minor variations in titles (e.g., punctuation differences).
Could verify PDF file type explicitly rather than just relying on .pdf extension.
